name: Qwen3.5-4B-Qwenputer
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: Inherited from Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B plus 11 compiled RISC-V layers in front of Qwen's own 32: hidden size widens from 2560 to 3968 and the vocabulary gains 230,324 trace tokens. 8 full-attention layers at indices 3,7,11,15,19,23,27,31 held against 24 linear-attention (Gated DeltaNet) layers, GQA 16 query / 4 KV heads, head_dim 256.
notes: ADDED 2026-10-31 from the trending sweep. Not a fine-tune of behaviour: 11 transformer layers holding a compiled RV32IM CPU are prepended to an otherwise unmodified Qwen3.5-4B, and the card states Qwen's own weights are unchanged and the config is only widened (hidden 2560 -> 3968, vocab +230,324 trace tokens). params_b 9.358 = safetensors.total 9,357,602,496, which is the widened file size, not a capability increase: the card says 18.8 GB in bf16 is 'mostly zero padding' and the computer has about 1M nonzero weights. active_params_b 9.358 because the stack is dense - every parameter is touched per token, so unlike an MoE there is no smaller active set. kv_cache_bytes_per_token 32768 is the 8 full-attention layers x 2 x 4 KV heads x 256 head_dim x 2 B; the 24 DeltaNet layers hold constant state and add nothing per token. flops_per_token_active left null: the base's value does not apply to a widened hidden size plus 11 compiled layers, and the card publishes no FLOPs. Evidence: 5 arithmetic rows where the card's own column beats the base column on the same 40 problems. Read the Python-tool column beside them - base Qwen3.5-4B with a real host interpreter matches or beats Qwenputer on 3 of the 5 rows, so this is an internal-tool-access result, not a smarter model. The 'merge' derivative_kind is what the card's base_model_relation says; it is really an architectural splice. Licence apache-2.0, repo created 2026-10-19.
